newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midcontinent unleaded rises on refinery talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midcontinent unleaded rises on refinery talk.

text.p: Spot refined product differentials in the U.S. midcontinent strengthened Wednesday following rumors Amoco had a refinery problem on the Gulf Coast, traders said.
"People were nervous about the refinery problems in the Gulf," said one product player, noting, however, market activity remained light.

There was talk Amoco had an operational problem at one of its Gulf refineries but the company would not comment on the status of its units. Amoco had been buying blendstocks in the Gulf spot market and selling conventional grade gasoline.
Amoco has been buying blendstocks in the Gulf spot market and selling conventional grade gasoline.

On the refinery news, diffs for Group Three prompt unleaded rose by a cent to 2.75/3.00 cents a gallon over NYMEX June gasoline futures. Any month material was up 0.75 cent to 0.75/1.00 cent over the screen.
Earlier in the day, an any 0.10 cent and 0.30 cent traded hands.
Chicago prompt unleaded diffs were also up a quarter to 0.75/1.00 cent over the screen. Anys were pegged a quarter higher.
Group Three spot premium was up a quarter 3.25/3.50 and Chicago market material held largely steady.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
